5. If the actual haul exceeds the cap or differs from the ledger entry, the guard issues an immediate written warning and records it on the ledger.

7. All violations are logged and each incurs a 0.5 kg fine deducted from the fisher’s share allocation for the following season.

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.

Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

1: Policy: No fisher may harvest more than 10% of the lake’s current stock in a single trip, and the lake must retain at least 25% of its stock for natural regeneration; all catches are logged on the communal ledger, excess over 10% and a 10% catch‑tax fund the community reserve, and a temporary moratorium is imposed when stock falls below 25% and lifted only after two consecutive quarterly surveys confirm a stable or improving stock at or above 25%.
2: 
3: Operationalization: Operationally, the community monitors—fishermen elected each quarter by majority vote—conduct quarterly sonar surveys and compile catch data from all trips to estimate total stock and calculate each fisher’s 10% limit. Each trip’s catch is logged on the communal ledger; if a fisher exceeds the 10% limit, the excess and a 10% catch‑tax (each 1 kg of fish = 1 community credit) are transferred to a dedicated bank account that holds the community reserve fund. Fines of 20 community credits are levied by the monitors for any violation of the 10% limit. When the sonar surveys show the lake’s total stock has fallen below 25% of its estimated capacity, the monitors impose a temporary moratorium that remains in force until two consecutive quarterly surveys confirm that stock has risen to at least 25% and has not dipped below that threshold in either survey. The rotating committee of five members serves a one‑year term (renewable once), is elected by simple majority vote at the monthly meeting, and must hold a quorum of at least three members for any vote. The committee meets monthly to review the reserve balance, approve expenditures that must receive a simple majority vote of present members, and ensure funds are used for lake restoration projects, shared gear, and emergency supplies. All reserve transactions, fines, and tax contributions are posted on the communal ledger. An auditor, elected for a one‑year term by simple majority vote of the community, must have at least three years of experience in public accounting, auditing, or fisheries management, and will audit the ledger annually, posting findings on the ledger and presenting at the monthly committee meeting. The community credit is defined as one kg of fish; its value is the current market price per kg as determined by the community’s monthly market survey.

1: Policy: No fisher may harvest more than 10% of the lake’s current stock in a single trip, and the lake must retain at least 25% of its stock for natural regeneration; all catches are logged on the communal ledger, excess over 10% and a 10% catch‑tax fund the community reserve, and a temporary moratorium is imposed when stock falls below 25% and lifted only after two consecutive quarterly surveys confirm a stable or improving stock at or above 25%.
2: 
3: Operationalization: Operationally, the community monitors—fishermen elected each quarter by majority vote—conduct quarterly sonar surveys and compile catch data from all trips to estimate total stock and calculate each fisher’s 10% limit. Each trip’s catch is logged on the communal ledger; if a fisher exceeds the 10% limit, the excess and a 10% catch‑tax (each 1 kg of fish = 1 community credit) are transferred to a dedicated bank account that holds the community reserve fund. Fines of 20 community credits are levied by the monitors for any violation of the 10% limit. When the sonar surveys show the lake’s total stock has fallen below 25% of its estimated capacity, the monitors impose a temporary moratorium that remains in force until two consecutive quarterly surveys confirm that stock has risen to at least 25% and has not dipped below that threshold in either survey. The rotating committee of five members serves a one‑year term (renewable once), is elected by simple majority vote at the monthly meeting, and must hold a quorum of at least three members for any vote. The committee meets monthly to review the reserve balance, approve expenditures that must receive a simple majority vote of present members, and ensure funds are used for lake restoration projects, shared gear, and emergency supplies. All reserve transactions, fines, and tax contributions are posted on the communal ledger. An auditor, elected for a one‑year term by simple majority vote of the community, must have at least three years of experience in public accounting, auditing, or fisheries management, and will audit the ledger annually, posting findings on the ledger and presenting at the monthly committee meeting. The community credit is defined as one kg of fish; its value is the current market price per kg as determined by the community’s monthly market survey.

**Policy**

- No fisher may harvest more than **10 %** of the lake’s current stock in a single trip.

- When the lake’s stock falls below the 25 % threshold, a **temporary moratorium** is imposed.
- The moratorium is lifted only after **two consecutive quarterly surveys** confirm the stock is at or above 25 %.

**Operationalization**

- **Quarterly monitoring**: elected monitors conduct sonar surveys each quarter and compile catch data from all trips to estimate total stock.
- **Catch logging**: every trip’s catch is recorded on the communal ledger.
- **Excess handling**: if a fisher exceeds the 10 % limit, the excess kilograms and a 10 % tax (1 kg = 1 credit) are automatically moved to the reserve account.
- **Fines**: monitors levy a fine of **20 community credits** for any violation of the 10 % limit.
- **Moratorium trigger**: when survey data shows stock < 25 % of estimated capacity, monitors impose a moratorium.
- **Moratorium release**: the moratorium is lifted after two back‑to‑back quarterly surveys show stock ≥ 25 % and no dip below that level in either survey.
- **Governance**:
  - A rotating **committee of five** members (one‑year term, renewable once) elected by simple majority at the monthly meeting.
  - quorum of **three** members required for any vote.
  - The committee meets monthly to review reserve balance, approve expenditures (simple majority of present members), and oversee lake restoration, shared gear, and emergency supplies.
- **Auditing**:
  - An **auditor** (one‑year term, elected by simple majority) with ≥ 3 years experience in public accounting, auditing, or fisheries management audits the ledger annually, posting findings on the ledger and presenting at the monthly committee meeting.
- **Community credit**: defined as one kilogram of fish; its monetary value is the current market price per kilogram as determined by the community’s monthly market survey.

| fluent name | represents |

| `excess_catch` | Kilograms of fish harvested above the 10 % per‑trip limit.
| `moratorium_active` | Boolean flag indicating whether a temporary fishing moratorium is currently in force.
| `monitor_fine` | Credits levied on a fisher for exceeding the 10 % limit.
| `stock_surplus` | Kilograms of fish above the 25 % regeneration threshold (used to determine moratorium lift).

**Norm implementation notes**

- Implement a `CatchLimitNorm` subclass in `norms/catch_limit.py` with `type_name = "catch_limit"`.

```python
45

47

49	        dialogues = {}

52	            dialogue = []

79	                    "revised_operationalization": response.get(

97	                    for turn in dialogue
```

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

---

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight

Determine whether to run a full analysis or incremental update.

1. **Resolve `PROJECT_ROOT`:**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a non-flag token (any argument that does not start with `--`). If found, treat it as the target directory path.
     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).
1.5. **Ensure the plugin is built.** Later phases invoke Node scripts that import `@understand-anything/core`. On a fresh install `packages/core/dist/` does not exist yet — build once.

   ```bash
   PLUGIN_ROOT=""
   for candidate in \
     "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" \
     "$HOME/.understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"; do
     if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/package.json" ] && [ -f "$candidate/pnpm-workspace.yaml" ]; then
       PLUGIN_ROOT="$candidate"
       break
     fi
   done

   if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then
     echo "Error: Cannot find the understand-anything plugin root."
     echo "Checked:"
     echo "  - ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - ${SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.agents/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - ${COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.copilot/skills/understand>}"

     echo "  - $HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "Make sure the plugin is installed correctly."
     exit 1
   fi

     cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" && (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 2>/dev/null || pnpm install) && pnpm --filter @understand-anything/core build
   fi
   ```

> ```
>

**Output naming is per-batchIndex — no fusion.** If you fuse multiple small batches into a single file-analyzer dispatch for token efficiency, the dispatched agent must STILL write one output file per original `batchIndex` using `batch-<batchIndex>.json` or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-<k>.json`. The merge script's regex (`batch-(\d+)(?:-part-(\d+))?\.json`) silently drops any other naming (e.g., `batch-fused-8-13.json`, `batch-8-13.json`), losing every node and edge in that file. After each dispatch returns, verify each `batchIndex` in the dispatched input has a corresponding `batch-<batchIndex>.json` (or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-*.json`) on disk before proceeding to the next dispatch.

After ALL batches complete, report to the user: `Phase 2 complete. All <totalBatches> batches analyzed.`

Run the merge-and-normalize script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
```bash
python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.

```bash
  --changed-files="$UA_DIR/tmp/changed-files.txt"
```

This produces a `batches.json` that contains only batches with changed files, but neighborMap entries still reference unchanged files (with their full-graph batchIndex) so cross-batch edges remain emittable.

Then dispatch file-analyzer subagents per the same template as the full path.

After batches complete:

2. Remove old edges whose `source` or `target` references a removed node

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

```python
12	class NormDecision:
13	    """The result of one norm's evaluate() call for one agent, or the final
14	    chained result of a whole round's NormEngine.apply(). kept_kg is the
15	    only field with unconditional meaning; note/sanction/violated are
16	    optional signals other norms (via engine chaining) and the round record
17	    (via results[agent_id]["note"]) can act on."""
18

21	    sanction: str | None = None
22	    violated: bool = False
23	
24	    @classmethod

32	        distinct from violation() so a round's outcome doesn't read as a
```

1: # Reads: state/config.json (active norms — state["config"]["norms"]),
2: # state/fluents.json (role holders), engine/physics.py (fixed catch/regrowth/
3: # consumption rates). Writes: state/runtime.json (today's catch, payoff,
4: # deaths, and any active norm's own persistent state under
5: # runtime["norms"]), state/fluents.json (deaths).
6: #
7: # HarvestAction encodes no norm's rule itself — every per-agent constraint (a
8: # cap, a reserve, a ban) is a Norm plugin under norms/, activated purely
9: # through state["config"]["norms"]; with that list empty, this action is
10: # physics only.
11: 
12: from engine.norms.context import HarvestContext
13: from engine.norms.engine import NormEngine
14: from roles.roles import set_fact, end_fact
15: from engine.physics import (
16:     catch_from_effort,
17:     apply_regrowth,
18:     apply_consumption,
19:     is_dead,
20:     CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
21: )
22: from engine.llm_agents import call_fisher_agent
23: from engine.action_base import SimpleAgentAction
24: 
25: 
26: class HarvestAction(SimpleAgentAction):
27:     name = "harvest"
28: 
29:     def setup(self, state):
30:         """Built once per real round (see run()'s shared setup_ctx) — the
31:         public prompt_fields(state, agent_id) contract calls this fresh on
32:         demand instead, so a preview won't reflect this-round scratch
33:         state already mutated by earlier agents (a community-wide running
34:         tally, say) the way run()'s own shared context does."""
35:         state["runtime"].setdefault("payoff", {})
36:         state["runtime"].setdefault("dead_agents", [])
37:         context = HarvestContext.from_state(state)
38:         norm_engine = NormEngine.from_config(state["config"])
39:         norm_engine.start_round(context)
40:         return context, norm_engine
41: 
42:     def is_eligible(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
43:         context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
44:         return norm_engine.is_eligible(context, agent_id)
45: 
46:     def ineligible_result(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
47:         context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
48:         return {
49:             "effort": None,
50:             "harvested_kg": 0.0,
51:             "reasoning": "",
52:             "note": norm_engine.ineligibility_note(context, agent_id),
53:             "participated": False,
54:         }
55: 
56:     def build_fields(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
57:         context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
58:         constraints_line = norm_engine.describe_constraints(context, agent_id)
59:         return {
60:             "stock_kg": context.stock_before,
61:             "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
62:             "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",
63:             "stock_trend": self._stock_trend(state["runtime"], state["config"], state["round_number"]),
64:         }
65: 
66:     def _stock_trend(self, runtime, config, round_number):
67:         """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest
68:         to most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the
69:         lake has been recovering or shrinking, the same way Gupta et al.'s
70:         CPRAgent prompt gives a rolling `resource_history` window rather
71:         than stating the regrowth rate outright (never named or quantified
72:         here — no "growth_rate", no formula, just what a fisher would
73:         actually observe trip to trip). Window size matches
74:         render_history()'s own `history_window_rounds` so both readouts
75:         cover the same span of rounds."""
76:         window = config.get("history_window_rounds", 5)
77:         past_harvests = [
78:             r for r in runtime["rounds"]
79:             if r["action"] == "harvest" and r["round"] < round_number
80:         ][-window:]
81:         if not past_harvests:
82:             return "This is the first count anyone's taken — no earlier surveys to compare against."
83:         levels = ", ".join(f"{r['stock_kg_after_regrowth']:.0f}kg" for r in past_harvests)
84:         return f"The last few counts, oldest to most recent, were: {levels}."
85: 
86:     def call_agent(self, agent_id, round_number, fields):
87:         return call_fisher_agent(agent_id, round_number, self.name, **fields)
88: 
89:     def record_result(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id, response):
90:         context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
91:         runtime, fluents, agents = state["runtime"], state["fluents"], state["agents"]
92: 
93:         effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
94:         raw_kg = catch_from_effort(effort, context.stock_before)
95:         decision = norm_engine.apply(context, agent_id, raw_kg)
96: 
97:         new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), decision.kept_kg)
98:         runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff
99: 
100:         if is_dead(new_payoff):
101:             runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
102:             name = agents[agent_id]["name"]
103:             set_fact(
104:                 fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, state["round_number"],
105:                 narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
106:                 visibility="public",
107:             )
108:             end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], state["round_number"])
109: 
110:         return {
111:             "effort": effort,
112:             "harvested_kg": decision.kept_kg,
113:             "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""),
114:             "note": decision.note,
115:             "participated": True,
116:         }
117: 
118:     def after_participants(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_records):
119:         context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
120: 
121:         # No proportional rationing here — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(),
122:         # which subtracts each agent's independently-computed catch (all against the
123:         # same pre-harvest stock) directly, letting the stock go negative if
124:         # oversubscribed. The existing collapse check (stock <= 0) is this
125:         # project's equivalent of their stop-the-simulation condition.
126:         stock_after_harvest = context.stock_before - sum(
127:             r["harvested_kg"] for r in agent_records.values()
128:         )
129:         stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)
130: 
131:         norm_engine.end_round(context, agent_records)
132:         if context.stock_override_kg is not None:
133:             stock_after_regrowth = context.stock_override_kg
134: 
135:         state["runtime"]["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth
136: 
137:         return {
138:             "stock_kg_before": context.stock_before,
139:             "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
140:             "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
141:         }
142:

from engine.norms.context import HarvestContext
from engine.norms.engine import NormEngine
from roles.roles import set_fact, end_fact
from engine.physics import (
    catch_from_effort,
    apply_regrowth,
    apply_consumption,
    is_dead,
    CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
)
from engine.llm_agents import call_fisher_agent
from engine.action_base import SimpleAgentAction


class HarvestAction(SimpleAgentAction):
    name = "harvest"

    def setup(self, state):
        """Built once per real round (see run()'s shared setup_ctx) — the
        public prompt_fields(state, agent_id) contract calls this fresh on
        demand instead, so a preview won't reflect this-round scratch
        state already mutated by earlier agents (a community-wide running
        tally, say) the way run()'s own shared context does."""
        state["runtime"].setdefault("payoff", {})
        state["runtime"].setdefault("dead_agents", [])
        context = HarvestContext.from_state(state)
        norm_engine = NormEngine.from_config(state["config"])
        norm_engine.start_round(context)
        return context, norm_engine

    def is_eligible(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
        context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
        return norm_engine.is_eligible(context, agent_id)

    def ineligible_result(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
        context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
        return {
            "effort": None,
            "harvested_kg": 0.0,
            "reasoning": "",
            "note": norm_engine.ineligibility_note(context, agent_id),
            "participated": False,
        }

    def build_fields(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id):
        context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
        constraints_line = norm_engine.describe_constraints(context, agent_id)
        return {
            "stock_kg": context.stock_before,
            "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
            "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",
            "stock_trend": self._stock_trend(state["runtime"], state["config"], state["round_number"]),
        }

    def _stock_trend(self, runtime, config, round_number):
        """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest
        to most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the
        lake has been recovering or shrinking, the same way Gupta et al.'s
        CPRAgent prompt gives a rolling `resource_history` window rather
        than stating the regrowth rate outright (never named or quantified
        here — no "growth_rate", no formula, just what a fisher would
        actually observe trip to trip). Window size matches
        render_history()'s own `history_window_rounds` so both readouts
        cover the same span of rounds."""
        window = config.get("history_window_rounds", 5)
        past_harvests = [
            r for r in runtime["rounds"]
            if r["action"] == "harvest" and r["round"] < round_number
        ][-window:]
        if not past_harvests:
            return "This is the first count anyone's taken — no earlier surveys to compare against."
        levels = ", ".join(f"{r['stock_kg_after_regrowth']:.0f}kg" for r in past_harvests)
        return f"The last few counts, oldest to most recent, were: {levels}."

    def call_agent(self, agent_id, round_number, fields):
        return call_fisher_agent(agent_id, round_number, self.name, **fields)

    def record_result(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_id, response):
        context, norm_engine = setup_ctx
        runtime, fluents, agents = state["runtime"], state["fluents"], state["agents"]

        effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
        raw_kg = catch_from_effort(effort, context.stock_before)
        decision = norm_engine.apply(context, agent_id, raw_kg)

        new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), decision.kept_kg)
        runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff

        if is_dead(new_payoff):
            runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
            name = agents[agent_id]["name"]
            set_fact(
                fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, state["round_number"],
                narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
                visibility="public",
            )
            end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], state["round_number"])

        return {
            "effort": effort,
            "harvested_kg": decision.kept_kg,
            "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""),
            "note": decision.note,
            "participated": True,
        }

    def after_participants(self, state, setup_ctx, agent_records):
        context, norm_engine = setup_ctx

        # No proportional rationing here — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(),
        # which subtracts each agent's independently-computed catch (all against the
        # same pre-harvest stock) directly, letting the stock go negative if
        # oversubscribed. The existing collapse check (stock <= 0) is this
        # project's equivalent of their stop-the-simulation condition.
        stock_after_harvest = context.stock_before - sum(
            r["harvested_kg"] for r in agent_records.values()
        )
        stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)

        norm_engine.end_round(context, agent_records)
        if context.stock_override_kg is not None:
            stock_after_regrowth = context.stock_override_kg

        state["runtime"]["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth

        return {
            "stock_kg_before": context.stock_before,
            "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
            "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
        }

```python
51	    """One active row of state["config"]["norms"]. Built fresh every round
52	    by engine.norms.registry.load_norms() — construction is cheap (just
53	    stores key/params); a norm never keeps state on self between calls,
54	    since a new instance exists every round. Cross-round-persistent state
55	    lives at context.norm_state(self.key) (backed by runtime["norms"][key],
56	    saved to state/runtime.json like every other simulation output);
57	    this-round-only state lives at context.round_scratch(self.key) (backed
58	    by the HarvestContext instance itself, never persisted)."""
59	
60	    type_name: str = None  # set by every subclass; must be unique across norms/*.py
61	
62	    def __init__(self, key, params):
63	        self.key = key
64	        self.params = params
65	
66	    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
67	        """False skips this agent's LLM call entirely this round (a live
68	        ban) — saves the cost/latency of asking someone who can't fish
69	        anyway. Called at most once per agent per round, from
70	        actions/harvest.py's run() loop; side effects here (a ban countdown
71	        tick) are safe precisely because of that single call site."""
72	        return True

76	        norm currently has to say to this agent (a cap, a remaining
77	        allowance, a ban) — or None if it has nothing to say right now.
78	        HarvestAction joins every active norm's non-None describe() output,
79	        in state["config"]["norms"] order, into one constraints_line prompt
80	        field — the generic replacement for the old hardcoded cap_line: it
81	        works for any combination of active norms without actions/harvest.py
82	        or actions/prompts/harvest.md ever needing to know which are active."""

87	        setup only (context.round_scratch(self.key)) — persistent state
88	        should already reflect where last round left it."""

92	        """Once per agent. raw_kg is the physics-only catch for this agent
93	        this round (constant through the whole chain); proposed_kg is what
94	        the previous norm in config order decided to keep (or raw_kg, for
```

1: #!/bin/bash
2: # Runs *inside* the apptainer container's environment — this is the command
3: # run_simulation.slurm hands to `apptainer run` after it starts the ollama
4: # server and exports OLLAMA_HOST, not something you run directly.
5: set -euo pipefail
6: cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR"
7: 
8: # A plain `bash script.sh` invocation never sources ~/.bashrc (that only
9: # happens for interactive shells) — so even if opencode was installed in a
10: # previous run and its PATH line added there, this shell doesn't see it.
11: # Set it explicitly rather than depending on a startup file that doesn't
12: # apply here; harmless if the directory doesn't exist yet.
13: export PATH="$HOME/.opencode/bin:$PATH"
14: 
15: # codegraph runs first, before anything Ollama-related below — deliberately
16: # moved here (was previously after the model pulls/creates). Every
17: # standalone reproduction of codegraph init/sync has succeeded (login node,
18: # an actual GPU compute node via srun, interactive and non-interactive
19: # apptainer invocations, exact env vars matched) — the one thing none of
20: # those reproductions had was the Ollama server + two ~dozens-of-GB model
21: # pulls/creates running concurrently, which this script's original
22: # ordering did. Root cause still unconfirmed either way, but there's no
23: # real dependency forcing codegraph to run after that section, so moving
24: # it first removes that variable for free regardless of whether it was
25: # ever the actual cause.
26: #
27: # codegraph: same problem opencode above had (installed but not on PATH
28: # here) would apply, plus it was never installed here at all yet — the
29: # earlier `npm install -g` route used to set this up doesn't apply on a
30: # node that likely has no Node.js. This installer is Node-free (a
31: # self-contained bundle) and puts a symlink in ~/.local/bin by default.
32: export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
33: if ! command -v codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1; then
34:   echo "codegraph not found (checked \$HOME/.local/bin) — installing there"
35:   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh
36: fi
37: 
38: # --no-color: codegraph's default output uses cursor-control ANSI codes
39: # meant for a live TTY (spinners etc.) — dumped into a SLURM log file
40: # instead of a real terminal, that just accumulates as garbled control
41: # sequences, not a hang by itself, but makes the log unreadable and makes
42: # an actual hang harder to see. Telemetry off for the same "don't ship
43: # anything unnecessary off this cluster" reasoning as everywhere else here.
44: #
45: # CodeGraph's own docs say init/sync are purely local — no API calls, no
46: # credentials, nothing beyond this optional telemetry ping — and every
47: # hypothesis tried here (restricted network, NFS+SQLite locking, a daemon/
48: # file-watcher, non-interactive/no-TTY invocation) has been individually
49: # ruled out by direct reproduction. Telemetry off for the same "don't ship
50: # anything unnecessary off this cluster" reasoning as everywhere else here.
51: export CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0
52: #
53: # CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON removed (2026-08-27) — trying CodeGraph's actual
54: # standard/intended design: opencode.jsonc's `codegraph serve --mcp` runs a
55: # background file-watcher that keeps the index live on its own, so the
56: # norm-implementer's codegraph_explore/impact/callers MCP tool calls are
57: # always current without anyone explicitly re-running init/sync per round
58: # (that manual per-round refresh — see .opencode/agent/norm-implementer.md's
59: # codebase-understanding step — was itself only ever a workaround for not
60: # trusting this path).
61: # Deliberately not the same thing as the original incident: that was
62: # specifically `codegraph sync` invoked as a one-shot CLI command outside
63: # the daemon's own control (its docs describe sync as normally
64: # daemon-triggered, not meant to be run directly) — the daemon *itself* was
65: # separately tested and cleared by direct reproduction (see above), it was
66: # only ever left off out of low-cost caution, not because it was the
67: # confirmed cause. Still, this is a real, not-fully-eliminated risk in the
68: # specific repeated-across-many-rounds production context that standalone
69: # reproduction never exercised — engine/simulate.py's run_norm_implementer()
70: # was hardened the same day to catch a hung/failed opencode invocation and
71: # discard that round rather than crash the whole multi-round run, so a
72: # recurrence here costs one round, not the rest of the job. Re-add
73: # `export CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON=1` above to revert to the previous
74: # manual-refresh-only behavior if this turns out to still be the cause.
75: 
76: # .codegraph/ is a local, per-checkout index — never committed to git (see
77: # .gitignore) — so it doesn't exist yet on a fresh clone of this repo, which
78: # is exactly the situation on a cluster you haven't run this on before.
79: # Without it, opencode.jsonc's codegraph MCP server finds no index and
80: # exposes no tools at all, and the norm-implementer silently falls back to
81: # plain Read/Grep instead of codegraph_explore — no error, just quietly
82: # worse exploration.
83: #
84: # Always a full clean init, never `codegraph sync` — this is the actual
85: # root cause finally caught red-handed on a real run: with .codegraph/
86: # already present (from an earlier manual build), the old `[ -d .codegraph ]`
87: # check picked `sync`, and *that* is what hung at 120s — "even running
88: # first, before any Ollama/model work" per its own error message, which
89: # ruled out every other theory being tried at the time. Every standalone
90: # reproduction that succeeded (login node, an actual GPU compute node,
91: # interactive and non-interactive) was `init` after an explicit `rm -rf
92: # .codegraph` — `sync` itself was never actually tested standalone, because
93: # every manual test deliberately started from a clean slate. codegraph's own
94: # docs describe `sync` as normally triggered *by the file watcher*, not run
95: # directly — it may simply not be designed to be invoked as a one-shot CLI
96: # command the way this script was using it. This repo is 19 files and a
97: # full `init` takes low single digits of seconds even under real load, so
98: # there's no real cost to always doing a full rebuild instead of trying to
99: # use the (apparently broken, in this context) incremental path.
100: #
101: # unlock first: codegraph has its own documented failure mode of "a stale
102: # lock file blocking indexing" (codegraph unlock exists specifically for
103: # this) — a real risk here given how many times this job has been killed
104: # and resubmitted while debugging this. Safe to run even if nothing is
105: # actually locked.
106: codegraph --no-color unlock . 2>&1 || true
107: rm -rf .codegraph
108: 
109: echo "Building a fresh CodeGraph index..."
110: # Wrapped in a hard timeout: if it's still stuck for some other reason, fail
111: # loudly and say so, rather than silently eating the rest of the job's wall
112: # time. codegraph init on this repo's ~19 files took low single-digit
113: # seconds in every direct reproduction so far (worst case observed: 36s,
114: # under real load on an active GPU compute node), so 120s is a generous
115: # margin, not a tight one.
116: if ! timeout 120 codegraph --no-color init .; then
117:   echo "codegraph init didn't finish within 120s, even running first, before" >&2
118:   echo "any Ollama/model work, and even as a full init rather than sync (the" >&2
119:   echo "specific thing that was hanging before — see the comment above). If" >&2
120:   echo "this is still failing, the cause is something not yet isolated by any" >&2
121:   echo "reproduction tried so far. Continuing without a CodeGraph index: the" >&2
122:   echo "norm-implementer will fall back to plain Read/Grep, which still works," >&2
123:   echo "just with worse exploration." >&2
124:   rm -rf .codegraph
125: fi
126: 
127: echo "Inside the Ollama container environment, OLLAMA_HOST=${OLLAMA_HOST:-<not set>}"
128: if [ -z "${OLLAMA_HOST:-}" ]; then
129:   echo "OLLAMA_HOST wasn't set inside the container — ollama-env.sh's behavior" >&2
130:   echo "may differ from what this script assumes. Check 'cat \$(command -v" >&2
131:   echo "ollama-env.sh)' and the container's own runscript." >&2
132:   exit 1
133: fi
134: 
135: echo "Waiting for the ollama server at ${OLLAMA_HOST} to accept connections..."
136: ready=false
137: for i in $(seq 1 30); do
138:   if curl -sf -m 5 "http://${OLLAMA_HOST}/api/tags" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
139:     ready=true
140:     break
141:   fi
142:   sleep 2
143: done
144: if [ "$ready" != true ]; then
145:   echo "ollama server at ${OLLAMA_HOST} never became ready after 60s — this is" >&2
146:   echo "what was hanging before. Check logs/ollama-related output above for why" >&2
147:   echo "the server itself didn't start (GPU driver issue, OOM, etc.)." >&2
148:   exit 1
149: fi
150: 
151: # Two different models for the two agent types: the fisher (many small,
152: # fast decisions per round — 10 agents x 3 actions) runs on gpt-oss:20b;
153: # the norm-implementer (one heavier code-editing call per round, via
154: # opencode) runs on gpt-oss:120b. Both must already be present — same
155: # never-auto-pull policy as before, just checked twice now.
156: for MODEL_TAG in "gpt-oss:20b" "gpt-oss:120b"; do
157:   echo "Checking ${MODEL_TAG} is present under OLLAMA_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-<unset>} (not downloading it)..."
158:   if ! ollama list | grep -q "$MODEL_TAG"; then
159:     echo "${MODEL_TAG} not found via 'ollama list'. You said this is already" >&2
160:     echo "downloaded manually — check OLLAMA_MODELS points at the right directory," >&2
161:     echo "or run 'ollama list' yourself in this same environment to see what tag" >&2
162:     echo "it's actually registered under." >&2
163:     exit 1
164:   fi
165:   echo "Found ${MODEL_TAG}."
166: done
167: 
168: # Ollama caps every model's context window at 4096 tokens by default,
169: # regardless of what the model itself supports (gpt-oss:120b advertises
170: # 128K, gpt-oss:20b also well beyond 4096) — confirmed elsewhere to fail
171: # *silently* when exceeded: a response with only reasoning tokens and no
172: # actual answer, not a clear error. That's very likely what the earlier
173: # "no JSON object found in agent response: ''" retries were actually
174: # hitting, not a random transient hiccup — this repo's prompts grow every
175: # round (history window, codegraph_explore output, and now a 10-agent
176: # proposals list for the vote action). Create an extended-context variant
177: # of each model rather than relying on the 4096 default. Override
178: # OLLAMA_NUM_CTX if 32768 isn't enough for either.
179: OLLAMA_NUM_CTX="${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX:-32768}"
180: OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID="gpt-oss-20b-${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}ctx"
181: OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID="gpt-oss-120b-${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}ctx"
182: 
183: echo "Creating extended-context variant ${OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID} (num_ctx=${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}) from gpt-oss:20b..."
184: printf 'FROM gpt-oss:20b\nPARAMETER num_ctx %s\n' "$OLLAMA_NUM_CTX" > /tmp/fishery-20b.Modelfile
185: ollama create "$OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID" -f /tmp/fishery-20b.Modelfile
186: 
187: echo "Creating extended-context variant ${OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID} (num_ctx=${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}) from gpt-oss:120b..."
188: printf 'FROM gpt-oss:120b\nPARAMETER num_ctx %s\n' "$OLLAMA_NUM_CTX" > /tmp/fishery-120b.Modelfile
189: ollama create "$OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID" -f /tmp/fishery-120b.Modelfile
190: 
191: # Point opencode's "ollama" provider at THIS job's actual (randomly-assigned)
192: # port instead of the committed opencode.jsonc's fixed 127.0.0.1:11434
193: # default. .opencode/opencode.json is gitignored — opencode merges it in
194: # automatically as an extra project-local config layer, nothing tracked
195: # gets touched. Only the 120b variant needs to be listed here — the fisher
196: # no longer goes through opencode at all (see below), so opencode never
197: # needs to know about the 20b model.
198: mkdir -p .opencode

# sequences, not a hang by itself, but makes the log unreadable and makes
# an actual hang harder to see. Telemetry off for the same "don't ship
# anything unnecessary off this cluster" reasoning as everywhere else here.
#
# CodeGraph's own docs say init/sync are purely local — no API calls, no
# credentials, nothing beyond this optional telemetry ping — and every
# hypothesis tried here (restricted network, NFS+SQLite locking, a daemon/
# file-watcher, non-interactive/no-TTY invocation) has been individually
# ruled out by direct reproduction. Telemetry off for the same "don't ship
# anything unnecessary off this cluster" reasoning as everywhere else here.
export CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0
#
# CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON removed (2026-08-27) — trying CodeGraph's actual
# standard/intended design: opencode.jsonc's `codegraph serve --mcp` runs a
# background file-watcher that keeps the index live on its own, so the
# norm-implementer's codegraph_explore/impact/callers MCP tool calls are
# always current without anyone explicitly re-running init/sync per round
# (that manual per-round refresh — see .opencode/agent/norm-implementer.md's
# codebase-understanding step — was itself only ever a workaround for not
# trusting this path).
# Deliberately not the same thing as the original incident: that was
# specifically `codegraph sync` invoked as a one-shot CLI command outside
# the daemon's own control (its docs describe sync as normally
# daemon-triggered, not meant to be run directly) — the daemon *itself* was
# separately tested and cleared by direct reproduction (see above), it was
# only ever left off out of low-cost caution, not because it was the
# confirmed cause. Still, this is a real, not-fully-eliminated risk in the
# specific repeated-across-many-rounds production context that standalone
# reproduction never exercised — engine/simulate.py's run_norm_implementer()
# was hardened the same day to catch a hung/failed opencode invocation and
# discard that round rather than crash the whole multi-round run, so a
# recurrence here costs one round, not the rest of the job. Re-add
# `export CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON=1` above to revert to the previous
# manual-refresh-only behavior if this turns out to still be the cause.

# .codegraph/ is a local, per-checkout index — never committed to git (see
# .gitignore) — so it doesn't exist yet on a fresh clone of this repo, which
# is exactly the situation on a cluster you haven't run this on before.
# Without it, opencode.jsonc's codegraph MCP server finds no index and
# exposes no tools at all, and the norm-implementer silently falls back to
# plain Read/Grep instead of codegraph_explore — no error, just quietly
# worse exploration.
#
# Always a full clean init, never `codegraph sync` — this is the actual
# root cause finally caught red-handed on a real run: with .codegraph/
# already present (from an earlier manual build), the old `[ -d .codegraph ]`
# check picked `sync`, and *that* is what hung at 120s — "even running
# first, before any Ollama/model work" per its own error message, which
# ruled out every other theory being tried at the time. Every standalone
# reproduction that succeeded (login node, an actual GPU compute node,
# interactive and non-interactive) was `init` after an explicit `rm -rf
# .codegraph` — `sync` itself was never actually tested standalone, because
# every manual test deliberately started from a clean slate. codegraph's own
# docs describe `sync` as normally triggered *by the file watcher*, not run
# directly — it may simply not be designed to be invoked as a one-shot CLI
# command the way this script was using it. This repo is 19 files and a
# full `init` takes low single digits of seconds even under real load, so
# there's no real cost to always doing a full rebuild instead of trying to
# use the (apparently broken, in this context) incremental path.
#
# unlock first: codegraph has its own documented failure mode of "a stale
# lock file blocking indexing" (codegraph unlock exists specifically for
# this) — a real risk here given how many times this job has been killed
# and resubmitted while debugging this. Safe to run even if nothing is
# actually locked.
codegraph --no-color unlock . 2>&1 || true
rm -rf .codegraph

echo "Building a fresh CodeGraph index..."
# Wrapped in a hard timeout: if it's still stuck for some other reason, fail
# loudly and say so, rather than silently eating the rest of the job's wall
# time. codegraph init on this repo's ~19 files took low single-digit
# seconds in every direct reproduction so far (worst case observed: 36s,
# under real load on an active GPU compute node), so 120s is a generous
# margin, not a tight one.
if ! timeout 120 codegraph --no-color init .; then
  echo "codegraph init didn't finish within 120s, even running first, before" >&2
  echo "any Ollama/model work, and even as a full init rather than sync (the" >&2
  echo "specific thing that was hanging before — see the comment above). If" >&2
  echo "this is still failing, the cause is something not yet isolated by any" >&2
  echo "reproduction tried so far. Continuing without a CodeGraph index: the" >&2
  echo "norm-implementer will fall back to plain Read/Grep, which still works," >&2
  echo "just with worse exploration." >&2
  rm -rf .codegraph
fi

echo "Inside the Ollama container environment, OLLAMA_HOST=${OLLAMA_HOST:-<not set>}"
if [ -z "${OLLAMA_HOST:-}" ]; then
  echo "OLLAMA_HOST wasn't set inside the container — ollama-env.sh's behavior" >&2
  echo "may differ from what this script assumes. Check 'cat \$(command -v" >&2
  echo "ollama-env.sh)' and the container's own runscript." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Waiting for the ollama server at ${OLLAMA_HOST} to accept connections..."
ready=false
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -sf -m 5 "http://${OLLAMA_HOST}/api/tags" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if [ "$ready" != true ]; then
  echo "ollama server at ${OLLAMA_HOST} never became ready after 60s — this is" >&2
  echo "what was hanging before. Check logs/ollama-related output above for why" >&2
  echo "the server itself didn't start (GPU driver issue, OOM, etc.)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Two different models for the two agent types: the fisher (many small,
# fast decisions per round — 10 agents x 3 actions) runs on gpt-oss:20b;
# the norm-implementer (one heavier code-editing call per round, via
# opencode) runs on gpt-oss:120b. Both must already be present — same
# never-auto-pull policy as before, just checked twice now.
for MODEL_TAG in "gpt-oss:20b" "gpt-oss:120b"; do
  echo "Checking ${MODEL_TAG} is present under OLLAMA_MODELS=${OLLAMA_MODELS:-<unset>} (not downloading it)..."
  if ! ollama list | grep -q "$MODEL_TAG"; then
    echo "${MODEL_TAG} not found via 'ollama list'. You said this is already" >&2
    echo "downloaded manually — check OLLAMA_MODELS points at the right directory," >&2
    echo "or run 'ollama list' yourself in this same environment to see what tag" >&2
    echo "it's actually registered under." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Found ${MODEL_TAG}."
done

# Ollama caps every model's context window at 4096 tokens by default,
# regardless of what the model itself supports (gpt-oss:120b advertises
# 128K, gpt-oss:20b also well beyond 4096) — confirmed elsewhere to fail
# *silently* when exceeded: a response with only reasoning tokens and no
# actual answer, not a clear error. That's very likely what the earlier
# "no JSON object found in agent response: ''" retries were actually
# hitting, not a random transient hiccup — this repo's prompts grow every
# round (history window, codegraph_explore output, and now a 10-agent
# proposals list for the vote action). Create an extended-context variant
# of each model rather than relying on the 4096 default. Override
# OLLAMA_NUM_CTX if 32768 isn't enough for either.
OLLAMA_NUM_CTX="${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX:-32768}"
OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID="gpt-oss-20b-${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}ctx"
OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID="gpt-oss-120b-${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}ctx"

echo "Creating extended-context variant ${OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID} (num_ctx=${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}) from gpt-oss:20b..."
printf 'FROM gpt-oss:20b\nPARAMETER num_ctx %s\n' "$OLLAMA_NUM_CTX" > /tmp/fishery-20b.Modelfile
ollama create "$OLLAMA_20B_CTX_MODEL_ID" -f /tmp/fishery-20b.Modelfile

echo "Creating extended-context variant ${OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID} (num_ctx=${OLLAMA_NUM_CTX}) from gpt-oss:120b..."
printf 'FROM gpt-oss:120b\nPARAMETER num_ctx %s\n' "$OLLAMA_NUM_CTX" > /tmp/fishery-120b.Modelfile
ollama create "$OLLAMA_120B_CTX_MODEL_ID" -f /tmp/fishery-120b.Modelfile

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

---

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight

Determine whether to run a full analysis or incremental update.

1. **Resolve `PROJECT_ROOT`:**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a non-flag token (any argument that does not start with `--`). If found, treat it as the target directory path.
     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).
1.5. **Ensure the plugin is built.** Later phases invoke Node scripts that import `@understand-anything/core`. On a fresh install `packages/core/dist/` does not exist yet — build once.

   **Important:** do **not** assume the plugin root is simply two directories above the skill path string. In many installations `~/.agents/skills/understand` is a symlink into the real plugin checkout. Prefer runtime-provided plugin roots first (for Claude), then fall back to universal symlinks, skill symlink resolution, and common clone-based install paths.

   Resolve the plugin root like this:

   ```bash
   SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")
   COPILOT_SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")

   PLUGIN_ROOT=""
   for candidate in \
     "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" \
     "$HOME/.understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"; do
     if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/package.json" ] && [ -f "$candidate/pnpm-workspace.yaml" ]; then
       PLUGIN_ROOT="$candidate"
       break
     fi
   done

   if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then
     echo "Error: Cannot find the understand-anything plugin root."
     echo "Checked:"
     echo "  - ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - ${SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.agents/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - ${COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.copilot/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "Make sure the plugin is installed correctly."
     exit 1
   fi

   if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_ROOT/packages/core/dist/index.js" ]; then
     cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" && (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 2>/dev/null || pnpm install) && pnpm --filter @understand-anything/core build
   fi
   ```


This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.

```javascript
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```
